vjimc-2000-cat2-01.prompt:
Let $p$ be a prime of the form $p=4n-1$ where $n$ is a positive integer. Prove that
$$\prod_{k=1}^p(k^2+1)\equiv4\pmod p.$$
vjimc-2000-cat2-01.answer: The squares $k^2$ run over $0$ (once) and every quadratic residue $r$ (twice), and $\prod_r(x-r)\equiv x^{(p-1)/2}-1$; at $x=-1$ this gives $\prod_r(r+1)\equiv2$, so the product is $\equiv 2^2=4$.

vjimc-2000-cat2-02.prompt: If we write the sequence AAABABBB along the perimeter of a circle, then every word of the length $3$ consisting of letters A and B (i.e. AAA, AAB, ABA, BAB, ABB, BBB, BBA, BAA) occurs exactly once on the perimeter. Decide whether it is possible to write a sequence of letters from a $k$-element alphabet along the perimeter of a circle in such a way that every word of the length $l$ (i.e. an ordered $l$-tuple of letters) occurs exactly once on the perimeter.

vjimc-2000-cat2-03.prompt:
Let $m,n$ be positive integers and let $x\in[0,1]$. Prove that
$$(1-x^n)^m+\big(1-(1-x)^m\big)^n\ge1.$$
vjimc-2000-cat2-03.answer: Colour each cell of an $m\times n$ board black with probability $x$ independently: \"some row is all black\" and \"some column is all white\" are disjoint events with probabilities $1-(1-x^n)^m$ and $1-(1-(1-x)^m)^n$.

vjimc-2000-cat2-04.prompt:
Let $\mathcal B$ be a family of open balls in $\mathbb R^n$ and $c<\lambda\big(\bigcup\mathcal B\big)$ where $\lambda$ is the $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Show that there exists a finite family of pairwise disjoint balls $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^k\subseteq\mathcal B$ such that
$$\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda(U_j)>\frac{c}{3^n}.$$
vjimc-2000-cat2-04.answer: Vitali covering argument: take a compact $K\subseteq\bigcup\mathcal B$ with $\lambda(K)>c$, cover it by finitely many balls, and greedily pick disjoint balls by decreasing radius; the tripled chosen balls cover $K$.
